cards.when: a binary outcome (a recession dummy 0/1); estimating P(y=1|x) from predictors (the yield-curve spread) with probit/logit; optionally high-dimensional fixed effects + clustered SE + weights
cards.when_not: a continuous outcome (-> #33, or forecasting); more than two categories (-> an ordered model, or #30); an endogenous dynamic recession state (a dynamic probit, outside the surface); counts (-> Poisson)

alternatives.criterion: you want an odds-ratio interpretation (probit is the Estrella-Mishkin default)
without high-dimensional FE / clustered SE it is equivalent
the recession state is latent/unobserved -> extract regime probabilities (gaussian/lm only)
an autoregressive latent recession probability (outside the wrapper)

output_key_fields: coefficients: named beta on the LINK scale (the index), NOT marginal effects/probabilities
coeftable: term/estimate/std_error/z_value/p_value (z-test; SE clustered if a cluster was supplied)
fitted_probabilities: P(y=1|x) via predict(type=response) — the score that feeds #84
obs_kept: 1-based indices of the retained rows (fixef/separation -> length < nrow; alignment)
pseudo_r2: McFadden pseudo-R2 (ratio of log-likelihoods, fitstat pr2) — NOT an OLS R2
loglik/aic/bic/deviance/nobs: fit stats; link/family/fixef_names: metadata
interpretation_traps: coef = the effect on the latent index, NOT the marginal effect on the probability (which shrinks at the extremes); only the sign & significance are directly readable
do NOT assume length(fitted_probabilities)==nrow; fixef/separation drops rows -> align through obs_kept
pseudo-R2 != R2; a McFadden value of 0.3 is excellent (not '30% of the variance')
perfect/quasi-separation -> coefficients of ±∞ with enormous SE, or a drop (check obs_kept & the SE)
an in-sample AUC (via #84 on the same sample) is optimistic; an out-of-sample/real-time vintage is needed
sources: Bergé 2018 CREA discussion paper (efficient estimation with many fixed effects)
Estrella & Mishkin 1998 Rev. Econ. Stat. 80(1):45-61 (probit recession probability)
Estrella & Hardouvelis 1991 J. Finance 46(2):555-576 (yield curve -> activity)
Kauppi & Saikkonen 2008 Rev. Econ. Stat. 90(4):777-791 (dynamic probit, alt)
McFadden 1974 (pseudo-R2)

cards.when: a numeric score/prediction (the fitted_probabilities of #83) + a binary target; threshold-independent discrimination: AUC + DeLong CI + the full ROC curve + the Youden best threshold
cards.when_not: >2 classes (multiclass); a point/interval forecast of a continuous variable (-> RMSE/DM, cat. 15); comparing two curves (roc_test, out of scope); calibration (-> Brier/reliability)

alternatives.criterion: a specific false-alarm/miss cost; you operate at one cutoff (-> best_threshold)

alternatives.alt: bootstrap intervals for sensitivity and specificity
alternatives.criterion: partial AUC or smoothed curves (outside the wrapper; the default is analytic DeLong)
an asymmetric cost, missed recession >> false alarm (Youden weights them equally)
comparing two models/curves (outside the wrapper)

output_key_fields: auc: Area Under Curve in [0,1]; 0.5=random, 1=perfect (the C-statistic)
auc_ci: {low,high,conf_level,method=delong}; low>0.5 -> significantly better than random
roc_curve: data_frame threshold/sensitivity/specificity (chart-ready; the ±Inf sentinels are removed)
best_threshold: named list at the Youden point (threshold/sensitivity/specificity; several rows on ties)
n_cases/n_controls: positives/negatives after dropping missing values; controls_level/cases_level: WHICH label is which
direction: '<' (controls below cases, the normal case for a probability score) or '>'; percent: False
interpretation_traps: CRITICAL label inversion: swapped control/case labels -> AUC=1-AUC; always read controls_level/cases_level; AUC<0.5 is often inverted labels/direction
direction=auto silently picks the orientation with AUC>=0.5, hiding an inversion; for a strict evaluation set direction='<'
an in-sample AUC (a predictor from the same sample) is optimistic; an out-of-sample/real-time evaluation is needed
Youden != operationally optimal (it weights false alarm/miss equally; macro recession-calling is asymmetric)
AUC measures discrimination, NOT calibration; the same AUC can correspond to very different probability calibration
sources: Robin et al. 2011 BMC Bioinformatics 12:77 (ROC curve analysis and comparison)
DeLong, DeLong & Clarke-Pearson 1988 Biometrics 44:837-845 (AUC variance / CI)
Youden 1950 Cancer 3(1):32-35 (index J, best operating point)

cards.method: High-dimensional k-way fixed-effects GLM (binary logit/probit, Poisson count) with an analytic incidental-parameter bias correction (Fernández-Val/Weidner) + average partial effects
cards.when: panel/pseudo-panel micro data with MULTIPLE high-dimensional fixed effects (e.g. unit + time; or a network: exporter + importer) and a binary/count response — the probability of a recession/default/transition per unit; you want a consistent nonlinear FE estimate with a CORRECTION for the incidental-parameter bias (short-T panels) + interpretable average partial effects with SE
cards.when_not: no fixed effects (a plain GLM or probit); a single fixed effect with few levels (a classic conditional logit, or #83, suffices); you only want fitted probabilities or an AUC with no bias correction (-> #83); a continuous response (linear fixed effects -> #33/#46); average partial effects for a Poisson model (not supported); interactions or polynomials inside the partial effects (not supported)

alternatives.criterion: you want a plain binomial FE GLM with fitted probabilities/clustered SE/pseudo-R2 and you do NOT care about the incidental-parameter bias correction (a long T or large groups)
you have a fitted (+ bias-corrected) binary model and you want interpretable average partial effects (marginal effects) + delta-method SE rather than log-odds coefficients
a continuous response — linear fixed effects rather than a nonlinear GLM

output_key_fields: coefficients (hdfe_glm): the uncorrected structural beta (log-odds or log-rate); coefficients_bias_corrected: the bias-corrected beta (absent when bias_correct=False)
coef_table (hdfe_glm): a matrix of Estimate/Std. error/z value/Pr(>|z|) for the primary estimate (bias-corrected when that was requested)
deviance / null_deviance / converged / iterations (hdfe_glm): the fit diagnostics (converged=False is blocked by a hard gate)
nobs (full/na/pc/effective) · fe_names · fe_levels (the number of levels per fixed effect) · n_fe · bias_term/bandwidth/panel_structure, when the bias correction ran
ape (hdfe_average_partial_effects): the average partial effects per covariate, in probability units; ape_se: the delta-method standard error; ape_table: Estimate/SE/z/p; vcov: the covariance matrix
bias_corrected / panel_structure / sampling_fe / weak_exo / bandwidth / n_pop (hdfe_average_partial_effects): the estimation settings
interpretation_traps: incidental-parameter bias: in nonlinear fixed-effects models with a short T the ML coefficients are biased; bias_correct=True gives the corrected beta — compare coefficients against coefficients_bias_corrected, where the difference is often 20-30%

the bias correction and the partial effects are for binomial models ONLY: a Poisson fit is estimated, but bias_correct=True and hdfe_average_partial_effects are rejected by a hard gate, since the partial effects support binary choice only

coefficients != marginal effects: the feglm beta are log-odds (logit) / z-scores (probit) — do NOT interpret them as changes in probability; use hdfe_average_partial_effects for interpretable average partial effects

bandwidth L: 0 only if ALL the regressors are strictly exogenous; with a lagged outcome (a dynamic panel / state dependence) set L=1.4 (Fernández-Val/Weidner); the order of the FE in the formula matters when L>0

panel_structure, network against classic: for bilateral flows (trade: exporter, importer, time) use network; the wrong structure gives a wrong bias correction and a wrong partial-effect covariance (the wrapper reads the structure back off the bias-corrected fit, for consistency)

perfect classification: the fit silently drops the rows and fixed-effect groups that are perfectly predicted (counted in the perfect-classification tally of nobs); check nobs so that you do not read a reduced sample as an error
non-convergence: converged=False (hard-gated) usually means linear dependence between a regressor and the fixed effects; revise the specification
sources: Stammann, A. (2018) Fast and Feasible Estimation of Generalized Linear Models with High-Dimensional k-Way Fixed Effects, ArXiv e-prints
Fernández-Val, I. & Weidner, M. (2016) Individual and time effects in nonlinear panel models with large N, T, J. Econometrics 192(1):291-312
Fernández-Val, I. & Weidner, M. (2018) Fixed effects estimation of large-T panel data models, Annual Review of Economics 10:109-138
Neyman, J. & Scott, E.L. (1948) Consistent estimates based on partially consistent observations, Econometrica 16(1):1-32 (the incidental parameter problem)
Cruz-Gonzalez, M., Fernández-Val, I. & Weidner, M. (2017) Bias corrections for probit and logit models with two-way fixed effects, Stata Journal 17(3):517-545 (average partial effects)
Czarnowske, D. & Stammann, A. (2020) Fixed Effects Binary Choice Models: Estimation and Inference with Long Panels, ArXiv e-prints

hdfe_glm (the PRODUCER; the fit + an optional biasCorr -> the object handle consumed by hdfe_average_partial_effects)

cards.when: the outcome has a natural order but no cardinal meaning -- survey scales, ratings, self-assessed categories
cards.when_not: the categories are unordered (-> multinomial); the proportional-odds assumption fails badly

alternatives.criterion: no natural order
ordered categories, proportional odds acceptable
proportional odds fails for some covariates

output_key_fields: params: coefficients, common across thresholds under proportional odds
thresholds: the estimated cut points
marginal_effects: per category, which is what is interpretable
brant_test: test of the proportional-odds assumption
interpretation_traps: THE PROPORTIONAL-ODDS ASSUMPTION forces one coefficient across every threshold, and it is frequently violated -- the Brant test is not optional
the coefficient sign tells you the direction for the highest and lowest categories only; middle-category marginal effects can go either way
thresholds are not parameters of interest and are not comparable across specifications
sources: McKelvey & Zavoina 1975 (Journal of Mathematical Sociology 4:103-120)
Brant 1990 (Biometrics 46:1171)
statsmodels.miscmodels.ordinal_model

cards.method: Count models: Poisson, negative binomial, generalised Poisson, zero-inflated and hurdle
cards.when: the outcome is a non-negative count, where a linear model predicts impossible values and misstates the variance
cards.when_not: the counts are large enough to be treated as continuous; the outcome is a rate with a known exposure and no count structure

alternatives.criterion: mean equals variance
overdispersion
more zeros than the count distribution allows

output_key_fields: params: count-equation coefficients on the log-mean scale, interpretable as semi-elasticities, one per covariate plus the intercept this node adds
rate_ratios: exp(params), which is the form a count model with an exposure is read in and the form published tables print
coeftable: term/estimate/std_error/z_value/p_value/conf_low/conf_high for EVERY estimated parameter, the zero equation and the dispersion included
dispersion: alpha, and null for a Poisson, which estimates none

zero_inflation: the inflation equation's coefficients, and null unless zeros='zero_inflated' -- a hurdle's zero equation is not an inflation and is reported in coeftable as zm_<covariate>, the estimator's prefix over this node's own design column names
vuong: NULL ON EVERY BRANCH. statsmodels 0.14.6 carries no Vuong test, so the statistic would be written in-engine, and no published value was found to check one against
fitted_values: the fitted mean per observation, on the scale of the counts, so the exposure is inside it
llf/aic/bic/nobs: fit statistics; family/zeros: which branch was fitted
interpretation_traps: OVERDISPERSION DOES NOT BIAS POISSON COEFFICIENTS but makes its standard errors far too small; the choice between robust Poisson and negative binomial is about inference, not consistency
zero-inflated and hurdle models mean different things: hurdle treats all zeros as one process, zero-inflation mixes structural and sampling zeros
an exposure variable belongs in the model as an offset with coefficient one, not as a regressor
sources: Cameron & Trivedi 2013, Regression Analysis of Count Data, 2nd ed.
Mullahy 1986 (Journal of Econometrics 33:341-365)
Lambert 1992 (Technometrics 34:1)
Vuong 1989 (Econometrica 57:307-333), doi:10.2307/1912557 -- the source for the promised vuong output field; statsmodels 0.14.6 carries no Vuong test

cards.method: Truncated and censored regression: Tobit and variants
cards.when: the outcome is observed only above or below a limit, or piles up at a corner -- hours worked, expenditure, bounded scores
cards.when_not: the limit is a genuine behavioural corner rather than a censoring of a latent variable; there is no censoring at all

alternatives.criterion: the latent variable is censored at a known limit
observations beyond the limit are absent entirely
participation and amount are separate decisions

output_key_fields: params: latent-variable coefficients
marginal_effects: on the latent variable, on the observed outcome and on the uncensored subpopulation -- three different things
sigma: the latent error standard deviation
censored_share: proportion at the limit
interpretation_traps: TOBIT COEFFICIENTS ARE FOR THE LATENT VARIABLE, not the observed outcome; reporting them as marginal effects overstates the effect on what is actually observed
Tobit forces the same parameters to govern participation and amount, which the two-part model relaxes -- and that restriction is testable and frequently rejected
Tobit is inconsistent under heteroskedasticity or non-normality, unlike ordinary least squares which is merely inefficient
sources: Amemiya 1984 (Journal of Econometrics 24:3-61), doi:10.1016/0304-4076(84)90074-5 -- eqs. (3)-(6), the standard Tobit model with its censored and truncated likelihoods
McDonald & Moffitt 1980 (Review of Economics and Statistics 62:318-321), doi:10.2307/1924766 -- the three marginal-effect scales
Wooldridge 2010, ch.17
a paper implementation: statsmodels 0.14.6 carries no Tobit and no censored-normal regression, so the likelihood above has no library to call

cards.method: Heckman sample selection, two-step and full information
cards.when: the outcome is observed only for a selected subsample, and that selection is related to the outcome
cards.when_not: selection is on observables only, where weighting suffices; no exclusion restriction exists

alternatives.criterion: transparent, easy to diagnose
efficient if the joint normality holds
selection is on observables

output_key_fields: params: outcome and selection equation coefficients
lambda_: the inverse Mills ratio coefficient, which measures the selection
rho: correlation between the two errors
exclusion: whether an exclusion restriction was used
interpretation_traps: WITHOUT AN EXCLUSION RESTRICTION the model is identified only by the nonlinearity of the inverse Mills ratio, which is weak and makes the estimates extremely fragile -- this is the single most common failure
a significant lambda means selection matters; an insignificant one does not license using the selected subsample if the exclusion restriction is weak
the two-step estimator's standard errors must be corrected for the estimated first stage
sources: Heckman 1979 (Econometrica 47:153-161), doi:10.2307/1912352
Puhani 2000 (Journal of Economic Surveys 14:53), doi:10.1111/1467-6419.00104

a paper implementation: statsmodels 0.14.6 carries no sample-selection estimator, so the estimator, its corrected covariance and its diagnostics have no library to call; the library supplies only the probit and the least-squares fit they are built on

cards.when: the outcome is a proportion or a share bounded in the unit interval, where a linear model predicts outside it
cards.when_not: the outcome is a count of successes out of a known total (use a binomial model); the bounds are not structural

alternatives.criterion: zeros and ones are present
the outcome is strictly inside the unit interval
there is a mass at the boundaries

output_key_fields: params: mean-equation coefficients on the link scale, keyed by term -- the intercept this node adds under the name const, and one entry per covariate -- each carrying its estimate, standard error, z statistic, p-value and the confidence interval at conf_level. The standard errors are the observed-information ones statsmodels reports, NOT the expected-information ones Ferrari and Cribari-Neto (2004) Table 2 prints

marginal_effects: the average effect of each covariate on the PROPORTION rather than on the link scale, computed as the sample mean of the inverse link's derivative times the coefficient, with no entry for the intercept. On the fractional branch it reproduces the library's own get_margeff(at='overall', method='dydx') to 5e-16 on all four links; the beta branch has no library answer at all, so the same arithmetic carries both

precision: phi on its natural scale where it is one number, the precision equation's coefficients on the log scale where precision_covariates make phi vary by observation, and null for model='fractional', which estimates no precision parameter
boundary_share: the proportion of observations at exactly zero or one, by exact equality rather than by tolerance, which is what says whether model='beta' was admissible at all
interpretation_traps: BETA REGRESSION IS UNDEFINED AT EXACTLY ZERO OR ONE; the common fix of squeezing the data slightly is an arbitrary transformation that changes results, so a fractional or inflated model is usually better
the fractional response estimator is a quasi-likelihood and is consistent under correct mean specification alone, which is why it is robust
coefficients are on the link scale and must be converted to marginal effects before interpretation
THE zero_one_inflated_beta MODEL IS REFUSED, not fitted: no implementation of the mixture exists to call, so a boundary mass has to be carried by the fractional model instead
sources: Papke & Wooldridge 1996 (Journal of Applied Econometrics 11:619-632)
Ferrari & Cribari-Neto 2004 (Journal of Applied Statistics 31:799)
statsmodels.othermod.betareg
validation_notes: model='zero_one_inflated_beta' must refuse with a GateError until a source is chosen: no zero-or-one-inflated beta mixture exists in statsmodels 0.14.6, whose statsmodels.othermod.betareg defines only BetaModel, BetaResults and BetaResultsWrapper, and no primary source for the mixture has been selected

the enum value stays because the node signature is frozen; dropping it is a contract change and an owner decision, and a branch quietly returning a plain beta fit under this name would be worse than a refusal

cards.method: Multinomial and conditional logit for unordered outcomes
cards.when: the outcome is one of several unordered alternatives -- sector, tenure, mode
cards.when_not: the alternatives are ordered (-> ordered choice); IIA fails and substitution structure matters

alternatives.criterion: chooser-varying regressors
alternative-varying regressors
IIA must be relaxed without a nesting structure

output_key_fields: params: coefficients relative to a base alternative
marginal_effects: per alternative, which are what is interpretable
predicted_probabilities: fitted choice probabilities
iia_test: Hausman-McFadden test
interpretation_traps: MULTINOMIAL LOGIT COEFFICIENTS ARE RELATIVE TO A BASE ALTERNATIVE and change entirely when the base changes; only the marginal effects and predicted probabilities are invariant
the marginal effect of a covariate on one alternative can have the opposite sign to its coefficient, because the probabilities must sum to one
an alternative chosen by very few observations produces unstable, sometimes divergent, coefficients
THE multinomial_probit MODEL IS REFUSED, not fitted: no implementation exists to call, so a substitution structure that the logit's independence assumption misstates has to be addressed another way
sources: McFadden 1974, Conditional logit analysis of qualitative choice behavior (Frontiers in Econometrics)
Train 2009, Discrete Choice Methods with Simulation

cards.method: Classification evaluation: Brier decomposition, log score, reliability and PR curves
cards.when: a binary or categorical model produces probabilities, and both their ranking and their calibration must be assessed
cards.when_not: the model produces hard labels with no probabilities; the classes are so imbalanced that every metric is dominated by the majority

alternatives.criterion: ranking, insensitive to class balance
the positive class is rare
calibration of the probabilities

output_key_fields: auc, average_precision: ranking measures
brier: with its reliability, resolution and uncertainty decomposition
calibration_curve: predicted against realised frequency
confusion: at the chosen threshold
interpretation_traps: ROC-AUC IS MISLEADING UNDER SEVERE CLASS IMBALANCE -- it can look excellent while the model is useless on the rare class; the precision-recall curve is the honest instrument there
a model can rank perfectly and be badly calibrated, and vice versa; the Brier decomposition separates the two
the classification threshold is a decision-theoretic choice, not a property of the model, and 0.5 is rarely optimal
sources: Brier 1950 (Monthly Weather Review 78:1-3)
Murphy 1973 (Journal of Applied Meteorology 12:595)
Saito & Rehmsmeier 2015 (PLOS ONE 10:e0118432)
